entries.en: We'll be taking her for counseling.
I wanted to save her. Stupid, huh? I mean, she was just a transport detail. But to see her so...
Right, uh,  you've got things to do. And I've got to collect her.
She's still back there, Commander.
Commander. Glad to see you.
Yes ma'am.
Yes sir.
Behind those shipping containers. I've got a sniper positioned, but I don't think we'll need him. She's only a danger to herself.
We've got a sedative to calm her down, but we can't get close to her. Every step we take gets her more wound up.
I-- I'm just doing my job, Commander.
Good luck, Commander.
Thank you again for the help.
I'll-- We'll take good care of her.
Is she all right?
Is it over, Commander?
I appreciate the help. But don't look down on her. She spent the last 13 years getting treated like an animal.
I'll take care of it from here. Commander.
Thanks, Commander. That means a lot. I didn't want to hurt her.
It's just, when I see her curled into a ball, shivering...
She was only six when they took her. Why the hell are we out here if we can't even keep one little girl safe?
Yes ma'am!
Yes sir!
So we clean up the wreckage, shoot the guilty, and hope everyone else learns not to mess with us. Great.
Will that ever be enough?
Thanks for your help, Commander. We are taking her to a counseling center. They'll help her get better.
I should have done something more.
I wish we could have saved her.
I-- I really didn't want to do that.
Please go, Commander.
She deserved a real life.
She's gone?
Yeah. Stupid question.
No. No, I understand.
I had to jump her to get the sedative in. I didn't see any other way.
Wish it were under better circumstances. Where is she?
Just tell me where she is, Lieutenant.
She's back there?
I hope I don't need it. Tell your men to stand by.
You seem awfully worried about her.
One way or another, she's coming out of there.
I'll talk to her. Keep back.
I'm fine. Thanks for asking. I got the sedative in her. She's out.
I just had to jump her to get the sedative in.
She took the sedative. She wants to get better, Lieutenant.
I got her to take her medicine. What a waste of my time.
I got her to take the sedative.
Bad things happen to good people, Lieutenant. That's why you and I are here. Don't wring your hands over her -- help her.
To make people who do these things pay. It's not the severity of punishment that deters crime, it's the certainty.
I don't have any answers for you, Lieutenant. We're doing what we can.
I'm sorry, Lieutenant. I couldn't save her.
You heard the gunshot, and I'm still standing here.
I did what I could.
I hope so.
"Is she all right?"
She's fine.
She's fine.
She's down.
It's over.
Don't lose heart.
To get the bastards.
I don't know.
I did the best I could.
What do you think?
Unfortunately.
I had to help.
Skip the pleasantries.
Where is she?
I'll take care of her.
Your concern
Give it to me.
I'll take it.
What's the situation, Commander?
I-- I don't think that's necessary, Commander. She's clearly no danger to anyone but herself.
But-- Aye, aye, Commander. I'll take care of her.
Thank you, Commander.
All right. Glad you're not rushing it.
Don't push her too hard. If she seems liable to pull the trigger, back off. Or walk away. I'm willing to wait her out.
This isn't working. You should take her out before she hurts anyone else.
You're really concerned about her, aren't you? All right. We're not down to last resorts. Just leave her alone for now.
I don't think that's your decision to make, Lieutenant. I want this docking bay clear in the next sixty seconds. You read me?
All right. This is your detail, Lieutenant. I'll play it your way.
No progress yet. I'm taking a break. Maybe she'll calm down a little.
Let her calm down.
I want you to shoot her.
No change.
Let her be, then.
Shoot her. That's an order.
If you're sure.
S-- Stop! What do you-- What are you?
Animals don't get names. The masters put their symbols on her. Hot metal all over her back. She screams when they do it.
It-- It happens to her. Doesn't it? They see her, so it's real. She doesn't want it to be real.
She doesn't want--
Happy?
The animals look at her funny. They look at her and she knows.
She's dirty and stupid. Broken. She doesn't talk good. She doesn't have clothes. She is an animal.
There's-- She sees them. They're yelling. Run. Hide. They hit the masters. But the masters, they have lights and hoses. Daddy's-- He's melting!
Sh-- She doesn't want to see that! Don't make her look. Don't look! Stupid, stupid!
When she thinks, water comes out of her eyes. The masters beat her when she wastes water. So she doesn't think anymore.
She's not strong. She's weak and stupid. All humans are. That's what the masters say.
Y-- Yes. She'll do better next time.
She sees them. Mommy and Daddy. Burning in white light. Melting. Going to pieces. They can't even say anything to her.
They're dead, Shepard. They try to save her, and the masters burn them.
Can she stop remembering now? Please?
No! She doesn't think about it! It doesn't happen! Daddy's at work. Mommy's making dinner. Go away!
N-- No! Ow! She doesn't want to go back!
She doesn't like needles. Wires. The masters made her sleep a lot.
It hurts when she-- when I remember me. But she wants to remember.
She won't ever forget. She won't be normal. Put her down. A spark at the back of the head.
Will you let her die? Please let her. She doesn't-- doesn't...
She remembers a lot of things.
Talitha. They call her that. Sh-- She doesn't remember the rest.
Leave her alone.
No! Stay back.
She-- I remember me. What I was before. But she doesn't want to remember anymore.
No! She's no good. Don't want to be handled again!
Will she have bad dreams?
She'd like that.
Lying. You get hit for lying. Get the buzz or the burning. Can't be there.
Why are you alive? Why are you-- Why aren't you like her? Broken. Only fit to dig and carry.
No. No one's lucky. Everyone's dead. Dead or an animal. It's not fair!
An animal that kills. Like the ones that made the masters explode.
She can't do that. She can't kill. Not to feel better about her past.
Dead animals can't work.
You lose your mommy and daddy. But you don't dig. You don't carry. You stand up.
She wishes she could stand up.
She can't escape. They have chains. Wires. Needles. You go too far, they take your brains away.
Animals like her come. Animals with guns. They make the masters explode.
She tries to fix the masters. So they won't be mad at her. She puts all the reds and purples back in, but they don't move. The other animals take her.
She doesn't want to see other animals. They're not real. They can't be real. They can't see her.
If the animals can see her, then this is real. But it can't be. The wires. The chains. The hitting.
This doesn't happen to her. It's another girl. A dirty girl. A stupid girl. She deserves it!
My name is Shepard. Lieutenant Girard sent me to talk to you. What's your name?
First, don't point that at me. Second, I'm Commander Shepard, Systems Alliance. Who are you?
What's the last thing you remember from Mindoir?
How did you get here? Did you escape?
The marines destroyed your world. As bad as it was, that was still the only world you knew. You didn't know them. They weren't safe.
You were afraid. All you'd known for 13 years was the "masters'" abuse. So you tried to heal them.
The marines who rescued you. They were the first humans you'd seen in 13 years. But you tried to heal your captors. Why?
Unbelievable. After everything they did to you, you wanted to help them?
You were rescued by Alliance forces. Didn't that make you happy?
What happened to your parents?
Listen to me. It's not your fault. You're not responsible. The slavers killed your parents. You didn't.
I know it hurts, Talitha. I'm sorry. But you need to deal with this. What happened to them? Think.
I don't want to hear that! You survived 13 years in a slave pen. You 're strong enough to deal with a memory.
Ignorance is stupid. Don't run from your past. Face it.
Tell me, Talitha.  You know where your parents are. You just don't want to face it. What did you see?
Hold still!
Shh. You're not going back. They're going to take care of you.
Sorry, kid. When you wake up, you'll be in a place where they can help you.
I couldn't take the chance you'd hurt yourself. It'll be all right.
Stay calm. I'll back up a bit.
I'm going to leave now.
My name is Commander Shepard. I'm an Alliance marine. I'm here to protect you. What can I call you?
You're not an animal. Your parents? What did they call you? Do you remember them?
I don't want to hear what those bastards called you. I want your name. The one you were born with.
You must have a name. A name you were born with. Can you remember it?
I'm going to take a step towards you now. Okay?
Talitha, this will make you sleep. If you fall asleep, they'll take you to a place where you can get better.
You'll dream of a warm place. And when you wake up, you'll be in it.
I'm not going to lie to you. I just don't know.
This is powerful stuff. You won't dream at all.
I was on Mindoir. My parents died in the raid.
An Alliance patrol arrived in system before they found me. The slavers never caught me.
For a while I was broken. I lost my whole family, Talitha. My friends. My childhood. I had to pull myself up and keep going.
I fought. My whole family fought, and got hit by an artillery strike for their trouble. I got buried under rubble. If they saw me, they left me for dead.
Some say I am broken. I kill aliens for a living. To protect humans from them.
We were trying to evacuate people. The slavers hit us with artillery. When I woke up, I was the only one alive. They must have thought I was a corpse.
Shepard.
Put the gun down.
An alliance soldier.
Think back.
Don't give me that.
You were born with one.
(Take a step towards her.)
(Give her the sedative.)
My childhood
The raid
Escape
Parents
(Use the sedative)
(Take a step back.)
Goodbye.
No.
I don't know.
No dreams.
The Alliance.
It was hard.
Nobody breaks me.
Who says I'm not?
I was lucky.
You were afraid.
Stockholm Syndrome.
You hid from humans. Why?
You helped your captors?
Alliance forces.
Don't blame yourself.
You need to face it.
Be strong!
Deal with it.
You know what happened.
It's all right.
You need help.
It's for your safety.
She's stupid. Stupid and chicken. That's why she's an animal. Stupid animal put in a pen.
Her mommy says there are no monsters. No real ones. When they come, there aren't any blankets.
She doesn't want to be there anymore. In the pen. In the cages. Lying quiet while they do things to her.
Please don't touch her. She's dirty. You'll catch it!
She doesn't want-- Don't touch her!
Fires. Smells of smoke and burning meat. Animals screaming as the masters cage them.  As they put the metal to their backs. Put the wires in their brains.
She pretends to be dead. If she's dead, she can't work. But they know. She hopes they'll leave. But they put her in the pen.
She didn't fight. She was already broken when they put the wires in.
She can. She can blame her. Stupid! She's stupid and she deserves to be dead!
She wants to believe that. She wants to believe nothing would change.
With everything that happened that day, no one could blame you for hoping they'd just go away.
Talitha, you were what? Six years old? No one blames you for staying quiet and hoping they'd go away. The only person blaming you is you.
You couldn't have fought them off when you were a child. They were bigger than you. There were more of them. They would have killed you.
All right, you didn't fight back. So what? I've been in combat. I've seen people make bad decisions under stress.
You were just a child when this happened. You can't blame yourself for pulling the blankets over your head and hoping the monsters go away.
You were scared.
It's not your fault.
The past is the past.
It was a bad call.
You were a kid.
Stay away from her.
